news.title: Players set to miss month of club football as congested schedule grows
news.lede: It is a never-ending debate in the football world – the schedule is too congested. Yet, there is talk that another major competition will be added to the women’s game and will potentially be plonked smack bang into the middle of the European club season. Fans had only just come to terms with the men’s FIFA World Cup ending and the club season had just kicked off when FIFA’s international window opened again. 24 of the 26 Matildas named to face Germany and Haiti play overseas.

news.title: Thomas Müller recounts Germany’s 7-1 win against Brazil in the 2014 World Cup
news.lede: Thomas Müller is never going to retire, is he? The Bayern Munich legend and Vancouver Whitecaps attacker recently featured on an episode of the Late Run podcast. In the episode, they look back at his career, and one of the main talking points was Germany’s incredible run in the 2014 World Cup and their ultimate victory. Specifically, Müller provided a behind-the-scenes look at their famous 7-1 win against Brazil.

news.title: Football: Portugal jumps into top 5 of Fifa world rankings
news.lede: FOOTBALL – Portugal was the only team that moved up in the top 10 of the updated Fifa/Coca-Cola World Rankings yesterday, climbing two spots to No. Brazil and Morocco each fell one spot in the only other changes within the top 10, after each drew a friendly during the just-concluded international window. Portugal won all four Uefa Nations League matches during this window, beating Norway twice and Wales and Denmark once each. Spain, fresh off winning its second World Cup this summer, built on its margin as the top-ranked team after sweeping the first four Nations League matches, beating England 3-2, Croatia twice and the Czech Republic.

news.title: Former Tottenham star announces plan to run against Gianni Infantino for Fifa president after World Cup sell-off shame
news.lede: FORMER Spurs defender Ramon Vega says he wants to stand against Fifa President Gianni Infantino. As European football’s top brass prepared to meet in Berlin to plot the next move in their fight against the world governing body, ex-Switzerland centre-back Vega, 55, became the first to actually put his head above the parapet. Vega accused Infantino and the current Fifa leadership of “demoralising” the game, blasting that “weak governance has damaged Fifa’s credibility and eroded trust across the global football family. “We must stop this conflict from escalating.”

news.title: A new equation shocks the football world: Yamal breaks the Messi and Cristiano barrier
news.lede: How did Lamine prove he is better than "the Flea" and "the Don"? In an era obsessed with numbers, Barcelona's gifted Lamine Yamal has chosen to answer the doubters in a language only the greats understand: consistency and impact. The 19-year-old is no longer merely a promising talent. He has become an unprecedented goalscoring phenomenon, achieving what Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland could not at the same age.
